title: Crown of Castile
capsule: The Corona de Castilla emerged as a unified entity in 1230 when Fernando III joined the kingdoms of Castile and León, and expanded dramatically through the Reconquista, incorporating Córdoba (1236), Seville (1248), and ultimately Granada (1492). Under the Catholic Monarchs Fernando and Isabel, Castile provided the institutional and financial framework for the first transatlantic voyages — Columbus's first expedition sailed under Castilian commission in 1492 — transforming the Crown into the center of an emerging American empire. The Crown of Castile as a distinct entity merged into the composite Spanish Monarchy upon the accession of Charles I (Holy Roman Emperor Charles V) in 1516, though Castilian institutions continued to govern Spanish America for three more centuries.
attestation: Boundaries from Seshat Cliopatria (Bennett et al., Scientific Data 2025; CC BY 4.0), digitized from standard historical atlases at ~0.07° resolution. Castilian Iberian territory is well documented through medieval chronicles and cartography; the Reconquista frontier zones are less precisely bounded in the earlier centuries, and the early colonial Americas holdings expand rapidly from 1492.
